near_far_convention: near = the jamb whose reveal the camera looks into, i.e. the wider of the two; far = the opposite jamb. Assigned per door from the measured band widths, cross-checked against the vanishing point of the head and threshold lines.
vocabulary: galvanised frame fixing lugs still exposed
characteristic: A basic door is one flat sheet with nothing applied to it: across all ten there is not a single window, grille, raised panel, inlay or piece of ironwork, and the only marks on the leaf are a peephole sitting at x 0.50 +/- 0.04, y 0.23 +/- 0.03 and one handle set at y 0.53 with its lock directly beneath - four of the ten add nothing more than a shallow perimeter or foot groove. What the tier does have is a frame painted the same colour as the leaf in ten cases out of ten and reading within 2% of its luminance, so the opening is legible only through geometry and shading: a near reveal of 0.051 of leaf width against a far reveal of 0.031, that near reveal falling from 1.00 at the head to 0.53 at the foot, and a floor contact line at 0.51 that is usually the darkest value on the door. Money in this tier buys hardware and installation, not shape - the cheapest two doors carry the same plain leaf as the dearest, and what changes with price is a lever-on-rose becoming a lever-on-plate, a raw concrete step becoming an aluminium or brass sill, and fixing lugs disappearing behind finished plaster.
